ARM E — PER-CLAUSE RETRIEVAL of the review list. Derived from ../list_in_prompt_insample/config_insample.json by exactly three changes: (1) system_files drops the 5th entry (40_review_list.md), because in this arm the list block is PER CLAUSE and is appended by run_arme.py using build_system's own '

---

' joiner; (2) output dir; (3) the cost cap. NOTHING under prompt/, schema.py, resources/, resolve_runs/graph_v2/, _debug_gen11/list_in_prompt/, _debug_gen11/list_in_prompt_insample/, _debug_gen11/examples_arm/ or _debug_gen11/selfreview_arm/ is modified or written by this arm; the four shared prompt files are READ from ../list_in_prompt/promptsB/ and never written.

corpus.description: a document-decomposition graph node: a single claim from the OpenAI Model Spec with assigned predicate names and its verbatim source text

select._: The 17 clauses of the ds_opus_loop — the SAME set arms C (in-sample) ran, so the comparison is paired clause-by-clause.

prompt._: The four files are arm B's, READ-ONLY. The fifth part — the review list — is built per clause by selector.py into promptsE/<clause_id>/40_review_list.md and appended by run_arme.py with the identical joiner. run_arme.py PROVES the assembly is production's by rebuilding arm B's system block from these same four files plus the FULL list and checking its sha256 against 04560828....
prompt._unused_files: The orphan guard fired here and was RIGHT to: promptsB/40_review_list.md is on disk beside the four files and is deliberately not sent WHOLE. Declaring it is how the config says the omission is intentional. It is not unused — a per-clause SELECTION from it is appended by run_arme.py, and run_arme.py refuses to send unless base + this file's full text reproduces arm B's system sha256.

cost._arm_e_cap: Owner-set hard cap for THIS experiment, $0.08. run_arme.py enforces it against the on-disk ledger before any send.

repair._: TURN 1 ONLY in this arm. max_attempts is never reached because run_arme.py issues exactly one call per clause and no feedback.

graveyard._: Not written by this arm — run_arme.py calls Client.complete_messages directly, as arms B and C did, and never enters translate's graveyard path.

execution._note: sync, not batch: 17 parallel one-shot calls, the identical protocol arms B and C used. Batching would change the latency profile and the arms would differ in more than the list block.
